title: Prediction of Customer Churn Behavior in the Telecommunication Industry Using Machine Learning Models
authors: Victor Chang, Karl Hall, Qianwen Ariel Xu, Folakemi Ololade Amao, Meghana Ashok Ganatra and Vladlena Benson
status: Algorithms 17(6), 231; author university repository and publisher record
review: The telecom study compares machine learning classifiers including Decision Tree and Random Forest and discusses LIME/SHAP explanations. It motivates comparing a simple tree with an ensemble and inspecting several error metrics. Our project instead uses validation permutation importance and a frozen test protocol. Published performance on a different dataset is not an Iranian Churn benchmark; the paper does not establish that its data cleaning matches ours.

title: A framework to improve churn prediction performance in retail banking
authors: Joao B. G. Brito, Guilherme B. Bucco, Rodrigo Heldt, Joao L. Becker, Cleo S. Silveira, Fernando B. Luce and Michel J. Anzanello
status: Financial Innovation 10, 17; publisher version of record
review: This banking framework emphasises RFM feature engineering and class-imbalance preprocessing rather than choosing an algorithm alone. It supports documenting preparation and minority-class evaluation. Unlike its transaction-scale sampling framework, our small aggregate-data project uses balanced classifier weights and no synthetic resampling. Its feature construction cannot be replicated from this CSV. Predictive ranking and segmentation remain different tasks in our implementation.

title: Customer segmentation application based on K-Means
status: Applied and Computational Engineering 47, 242-247; publisher record
review: This paper reviews customer segmentation applications and introduces K-Means with RFM-style analysis. It motivates an interpretable grouping task alongside prediction, but does not justify treating a cluster ID as a churn label. Our telecom usage features are not transactional RFM. We evaluate distance-based groups using training silhouette, inertia and minimum size, and name them from training characteristics rather than assumed marketing value.

title: Optimizing Customer Segmentation in Online Retail Transactions through the Implementation of the K-Means Clustering Algorithm
authors: Desi Adrianti Awaliyah, Budi Prasetiyo, Rini Muzayanah and Apri Dwi Lestari
status: Scientific Journal of Informatics 11(2), 539-548; publisher record
review: This retail study combines RFM-oriented customer analysis with K-Means and an elbow diagnostic, reporting three groups for its data. It supports examining inertia and feature profiles rather than reporting only a cluster count. Our reproducible training silhouette rule selects its own k and does not import the paper's three-group result. Feature scaling, category encoding and data populations differ, so numerical quality measures are not directly comparable.

title: Analisis Pola Dan Prediksi Churn: Hybrid Segmentasi SOM+K-Means Dan Klasifikasi Machine Learning
review: The study separates a SOM plus K-Means grouping stage from supervised classification and uses cluster labels as classifier inputs. It highlights the distinction between segmentation and outcome prediction. Our architecture is deliberately simpler: no SOM, resampling or cluster-label feature is added to the churn classifiers. Segments are a parallel descriptive output. Churn rates are attached by split only after fitting and never choose k.
